bibl.author: Henrietta Thomas and Sandra K. Bjerke [transcriber]

projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with John Aaron, Jr. was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: H. Marie Thomas. I'm speaking with -- what's your name?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: John Aaron, Jr.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: John Aaron, Jr. And you got your information on here, your birth date. I've got your address and information. I need the birth date.

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: [Birth date redacted].

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay. August. And where were you born, city of birthplace?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: Little Rock, Arkansas

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: All right. Okay. What branch of service were you in?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: I was in the Navy first.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: You said first?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: Yes. I was in the Navy from 1941 to 1945. Then I went in the Reserve in -- I went back to school, and then in 1957 I received a commission, second lieutenant in the Army.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Was that your highest ranking?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: I retired as a major.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Oh, okay. Okay. Do you remember your serial number?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: Which one? You know, your social security number -- is this -- this is something you don't give out. Is this --

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: No. It says serial number for service. It's different than social security number. Okay. That's fine. What battalion, regiment or division were you in?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: I was in the Navy. The first -- I was in the Navy. And I was stationed at the Naval Academy in Annapolis, Maryland in 1941 to 1942. And I was in Europe from '43 to '45.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: Stationed in Europe. I was with the 7th Beach Battalion.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: 7th?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: 7th Beach Battalion.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay. And which war was this you served in?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: That's World War II --

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: -- first. I was in the Vietnam War.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Did you sustain any service-related injuries while you were in the service?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: Well, yeah. I got disability now.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: You were not a prisoner of war.

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Do you have medals, awards and things that you could share?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: Yeah. Well, that's a big question; that I should have received the Bronze Star, but for some reason they gave me the ARCOM. So, in fact, I have, you know, sent a letter to the effect, you know, why I didn't receive the Bronze Star.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: Because everyone in my unit, you know, received a Bronze Star.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: And all -- also the unit received.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay. And you did receive -- what medal was that?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: ARCOM.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: What's that?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: Yeah, that's a lower, one lower down from the Bronze Star.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay. Just a couple of things. They wanted to kind of see what your service was like. Were you drafted or did you enlist?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: I enlist.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay. Where were you living at the time that you went in the service?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: Well, I went in the Navy from Little Rock, Arkansas, and I went in the Army from Chicago, Illinois.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: And did you pick the branch of service that you went in, or was that chosen for you?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: Yeah, I picked the branch of service in the Army.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: In the Navy I was a steward. But it's a funny thing. I was sent to Maryland and I was part of the staff on the USS Cumberland, which was a company ship next to the university. And what it was, the fellows on the Cumberland, they worked in the dining hall, the Vandercroft Hall, but when I went there they put me on the deck force. So I -- instead of going to the dining hall, I went and worked on the ship in the deck force. And then I went to school, and after I finished the course in school I was shipped overseas to England. I was in World War II and went to a place called Salcombe, South Devon. So I was there, you know, until the war was over.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: What would be your most memorable experience in your service?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: Kind of a lot of memorable experiences, but in the Navy I guess I was just a young man and, you know, right out of high school and, you know, never experienced being away from home. And I guess that's -- you know, I always think about that, but I never -- got my home training, so I never was -- got with bad company. You know, I was just fortunate enough to be accepted in the civilian area, you know. And I just enjoyed it because I was, you know, a young man.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: I spent -- well, it was two years in Europe and two years here. And I guess one of the most memorable things after I got a commission, and my family, we went to Italy. We was in Italy for three years. And I was able to take my wife back to England where I was stationed in the Navy and visit some of the people that I met there. That was really something. And my last daughter, she was born in Italy, and I have a granddaughter who was born in Italy.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay. Have you joined any veterans' organizations since the end of the war?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: Oh, yes.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay. What was your career after the war? What did you do after the war?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: I was a nurse in the operating room.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay. Is there anything else you would like to share that you think would be interesting about your career there or after your service?

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: Well, the only thing, I never had a bad moment. You know, I had a pretty good assignment. Even when I was -- you know, during the war in Vietnam. When I came back and was assigned to Fitzsimons, and then from Fitzsimons to Fort Benjamin Harrison where I retired.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Oh, okay.

sp.speaker: John Aaron, Jr.
sp.p: And I was able to enjoy it because I had my family with me. And we decided to stay here in Indianapolis after I retired.

sp.speaker: Henrietta Thomas
sp.p: Okay.
